preamble: The development of a glottal stop into the vowel [i] is uncommon. Its clearest case is Indo-Iranian, where PIE laryngeals between or after consonants were vocalized to *i; *h₁ is often reconstructed as [ʔ]. Loss of a postvocalic hamza with compensatory lengthening (Arabic biʔr > Maltese bir /biːr/) is ʔ → ː rather than ʔ → i, and simply dropping an onset glottal stop before /i/ (German [ʔiːɡl̩] ~ [iːɡl̩]) is ʔ → ∅; neither is counted here.

examples.note: The interconsonantal laryngeal *h₁ (possibly [ʔ]) is vocalized to i in Indo-Iranian. Compare Greek θετός, where the same laryngeal gives e.
The same *h₁ > i development; compare Latin genitor and Greek γενέτωρ.
